rca of the issue: Bug: GET /api/payments/vehicle-buy-now-checkout → 500 Internal Server Error. RCA: The except clause at /app/backend/routes/payments.py:2121 catches `stripe.error.CardError`, but Stripe SDK v8+ no longer exposes the legacy `stripe.error` submodule — error classes were promoted to top-level (`stripe.CardError`, `stripe.StripeError`, etc.). When Python evaluates the except expression at function execution time, attribute access fails (AttributeError: module 'stripe' has no attribute 'error'). Reproduction: any authenticated POST to /api/payments/vehicle-buy-now-checkout with a valid listing_id triggers it (the failure happens regardless of whether Stripe would have raised CardError, because Python resolves except classes during stack unwind). Mitigation: 1-line fix `except stripe.CardError as ce`. Add a regression test that ensures the route reaches Stripe (200/4xx, not 500 AttributeError). Also recommend a project-wide grep for `stripe.error.` to catch sibling references.
